reason: Both plans satisfy the phasing, risk-line, halt-threshold, and decommissioning-separation requirements, but Response A goes further by adding a fully gated post-migration decommission phase with concrete entry criteria (30-day soak, audit sign-off, read-only standby) while still keeping it strictly separate from the final migration batch, giving a more complete end-to-end lifecycle plan. It also includes finer-grained phase segmentation (canary/early adopters/GA ramp/final batch) and more concrete operational detail (e.g., a quantified 15-minute rollback SLA), making it marginally more actionable than Response B, which explicitly punts decommissioning out of scope entirely.
